transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Good morning, Mr. Thompson. I want to talk with you about your MRI scan and your upcoming surgery.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Oh, hello. Is it time for the operation?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Not quite yet. First, I need to tell you that a mistake was made. Two patients' scans were saved under the same identification number in our system. Because of that, our team looked at the wrong scan when we were planning how to do your surgery.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: What do you mean? I had the picture taken.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Yes, you did. But the computer showed us another person's image instead of yours. Does that make sense so far?

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I don't follow. You saw someone else?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Yes. We looked at the wrong image. We used that wrong image to decide how to operate on you.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Why would that happen? I thought you people were professionals.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: It was a failure in how we organized the files. I am sorry for any confusion this has caused. We have been incredibly busy on the ward lately.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Well, that doesn't help me. Am I in danger?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We have now found your correct scan. The good news is that we have corrected the plan. But I realize this is upsetting news to hear.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Upsetting? I'm just confused. I don't understand why you're telling me this now.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I want to be honest about what happened. It is a very frustrating situation.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I just wanted to get this over with. My hip has been hurting for months.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I hear you. It is a lot to take in when you just want to feel better.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: So, does this mean the surgery is cancelled?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: No, the surgery is still happening. We have the right image now, and the surgeon has reviewed it. To make sure we are on the same page, can you tell me what you understood about the mistake I mentioned?

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: You looked at the wrong picture. Someone else's picture.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: That's correct.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: And you're sorry about the confusion.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Yes, I am.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: What happens now?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Here is the plan. I have already updated your chart with the correct images. The lead surgeon is going to review the new plan one more time this afternoon. I will come back to your room at 4:00 PM today to tell you the exact time of your surgery tomorrow.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: 4 o'clock. Right. Do I need to do anything?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Your only job right now is to keep fasting from midnight tonight, just as we planned.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I can do that. I'm used to not eating.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I appreciate that. I'll be back at 4:00.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Alright. Thank you, doctor.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: You're welcome, Mr. Thompson.

H.justification: The resident allows the patient to finish their turns and adjusts pacing to the patient's confusion and distress.

E.justification: The error was named explicitly in the second turn using lay language, and a comprehension check was performed once.

A.justification: A direct apology was offered, but it was diluted by an excuse regarding being 'incredibly busy on the ward lately'.

R.justification: The resident named specific emotions ('upsetting', 'frustrating') and referenced the patient's desire to feel better.

T.justification: The resident provided specific next steps with a timeline (4:00 PM) and a named patient role (fasting), but did not address prevention.
